goal: One cart or checkout render works the basket out once, reads the customer, the cart count and stock once each, and sends no statement about bonus, referrals or checkout rules for a store that does not use them.
why: Today the cart page calls cartSummary() twice per view and each call sends 5 statements to learn that bonus, referrals and checkout rules are not in use; getCustomer(), getCartCount() and stock are read two to four times in one render. After: one summary per render, one read each, and none for a feature that is off.

commits.title: The customer, the cart count and stock are read once a render

changes.how: In getCustomer() (line 454) keep the two first lines (read the cookie; return null without a token) and run the rest (the session statement and the mapping) through `perRequest(`customer:${storeId}:${sha256(token)}`, async () => { … })` (import perRequest from './request-memo'). The token's hash is in the key on purpose: after a sign-in in the same request the cookie holds a new token, so the old answer is never reused; after a sign-out there is no token and the function returns null before the memo.

Line 26: `const count = await perRequest(`cart-count:${storeId}:${market.slug}`, () => getCartCount({ storeId, market }));` (import perRequest from '@/server/request-memo'). The header's link and the phone bar's then share one count. Do not put the memo inside getCartCount() itself: actions call it after they change the cart.
Line 62: `const customer = await getCustomer(store.id);` (drop the file's own `visibility:customer:` key; getCustomer() shares its read now).

Add near the top `const stockOnce = (storeId: string, ids: string[]) => perRequest(`stock:${storeId}:${[...ids].sort().join(",")}`, () => getVariantStock(storeId, ids));` and use it at the two call sites of getVariantStock() (ProductJsonLdSection about line 694, and the buy part's Promise.all about line 1012; both pass the product's variant ids). Stock is still read per request and never cached across requests: perRequest lives for one render only.

A unit test that one render shares the reads. React's cache() does nothing outside a server render, so stand in for one render: `vi.mock('react', async (original) => ({ ...(await original<typeof import('react')>()), cache: <T>(make: () => T) => { let made: T | undefined; let has = false; return () => (has ? (made as T) : ((has = true), (made = make()))); } }))`. Mock 'server-only' to {}. Mock 'next/headers' so cookies() returns a jar whose get(name) gives { value: 'tok' } for any name. Mock '@/db/client' so db() and readDb() return an object whose `execute` is a vi.fn() resolving to [{ id: 'c1', email: 'a@example.com', name: '', phone: null, address: null, has_password: false, company_name: null, organisation_number: null, avatar_path: null }]. Case 1: call getCustomer('s1') twice (await both) and expect execute called once and both answers equal. Case 2: getCustomer('s1') then, with the jar now returning { value: 'other' }, getCustomer('s1') again: execute called twice (a new session is read). If getCustomer imports modules that cannot load in a unit test, mock them as src/app/s/[store]/[market]/account/privacy/actions.test.ts mocks its server imports.

commits.title: The cart and the checkout work the basket out once, and ask nothing of a feature that is off

changes.how: Export `cartBonusOff(signedIn: boolean): CartBonus` returning exactly the object cartBonusOf() returns today when `!program.on` (src/server/bonus.ts lines 402 to 414: enabled false, signedIn, every amount 0, pendingAvailableAt null, earnPercent 0, pendingDays 0). In src/server/bonus.ts make cartBonusOf() return `cartBonusOff(signedIn)` there, so there is one 'off' shape. Also export from src/server/bonus.ts `bonusProgramOff(market)`: the BonusProgram value bonusProgram() returns for a store with the programme off (read bonusProgram() at line 69 and build the same object from its defaults without a statement: `on: false`, the default settings, the market's currency, no rates).

(1) Add `features?: FeatureSource` to cartSummary()'s third parameter (the `who` object). At the line `const program = await bonusProgram(db(), storeId);` (about line 99) use `const program = who.features && !featureOn(who.features, "bonus") ? bonusProgramOff(market) : await bonusProgram(db(), storeId);`. At the next line, when `who.features && !featureOn(who.features, "referrals")`, set `friend = null` and call neither codeInPlay() nor friendState(). Without `features` everything reads as today. (2) At line 82 pass `cachedRules: true` in the options of checkoutRuleOutcome() (see the checkout-rules.ts entry). (3) Add `export function requestCartSummary(store: Store, market: Market)`: `perRequest(`cart-summary:${store.id}:${market.slug}`, async () => { const shop = { storeId: store.id, market }; const cart = await getCart(shop); const summary = cart.lines.length === 0 ? null : await cartSummary(shop, cart, { features: store }); return { cart, summary }; })`. Server actions keep calling cartSummary() directly: they read after they write. Do NOT touch placeOrder() in src/server/checkout.ts: it reads the switches and settings inside its own transaction.

Add `export const checkoutRulesTag = (storeId: string) => `checkout-rules:${storeId}`;` and `async function enabledRulesCached(storeId: string): Promise<CheckoutRule[]>` whose body starts with 'use cache', then cacheLife('hours') and cacheTag(checkoutRulesTag(storeId)) (written as src/server/catalog.ts lines 285 to 287), and returns `activeRules(readDb(), storeId)`. checkoutRuleOutcome() takes a new option `cachedRules?: boolean` in its last parameter object: `const rules = cachedRules ? await enabledRulesCached(storeId) : await activeRules(runner, storeId);`. Only cart-summary.ts passes it; placeOrder() (src/server/checkout.ts line 561) and src/server/delivery-options.ts line 683 keep the live read. In the four writers saveCheckoutRule(), switchCheckoutRule(), moveCheckoutRule() and deleteCheckoutRule(), after the write succeeds, call `refreshTag(checkoutRulesTag(member.store.id))` (import from './refresh').

In loadCartView() (lines 71 to 80; if step 0.16 moved it, the same function in ./cart-view.ts): replace the first `getCart(...)` and the `cartSummary(...)` of the Promise.all by `const { cart, summary: known } = await requestCartSummary(store, market);` (buyer still read beside it); return the empty view when `cart.lines.length === 0`; `const summary = known!;`. Take `readCartBonus(store, market)` out of the Promise.all and use `const bonus = summary.bonus;` (cartSummary() already returns it, built by the same cartBonusOf()). Remove the readCartBonus import from this file. The perRequest key of cartView() stays.

Line 73: `const bonus = featureOn(store, "bonus") ? ((await requestCartSummary(store, market)).summary?.bonus ?? null) : cartBonusOff(false);` and remove the readCartBonus import if unused. First check that the credits part of the checkout draws nothing while `bonus.enabled` is false and reads nothing else of it; if it does, stop. At line 465 pass the known summary: `deliveryView({ storeId: store.id, market }, cartId, m.shipping, (await requestCartSummary(store, market)).summary)`.

deliveryView() takes an optional fourth parameter `known?: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof cartSummary>> | null`; line 23 becomes `const summary = known ?? (await cartSummary(shop, await getCart(shop), { cartId, customerId }));`. Other callers are unchanged.

The file mocks ./bonus and asserts `expect(readCartBonus).toHaveBeenCalledWith(store, market)` (line 209). Change the bonus cases (lines 204 to 231) to feed the bonus through the mocked summary (`summary({ bonus: bonus({...}) })`, as the file's summary helper allows; add a `bonus` field to that helper if it has none) and replace that assertion by `expect(readCartBonus).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. Mock '@/server/cart-summary' so that requestCartSummary returns { cart, summary } from the same fixtures and cartSummary is a vi.fn(); add a case: rendering CartLines, CartSummary and CartCheckout of one store in one test calls the summary once (with the stand-in for React's cache from src/server/request-shared.test.ts). This is the one existing test the step is allowed to change, because it asserts the call being removed.

A unit test of cartSummary() with features ['shop']: mock 'server-only', '@/db/client', './bonus' (bonusProgram: vi.fn(), bonusProgramOff and cartBonusOf passing through simple stubs), './affiliates' (codeInPlay: vi.fn(), friendState: vi.fn()), './checkout-rules' (checkoutRuleOutcome resolving NO_RULES) and the other server imports cartSummary() reaches (see how src/app/s/[store]/[market]/cart/cart-contents.test.ts mocks a cart). Call cartSummary(shop, cartWithOneLine, { customerId: null, cartId: 'c1', features: ['shop'] }) and expect bonusProgram, codeInPlay and friendState not to have been called. A second call with features ['shop', 'bonus', 'referrals'] expects bonusProgram called once. If cartSummary() cannot be loaded with mocks in reasonable size (more than about 15 mocked modules), write the same two cases as an int test in src/server/cart-summary-features.int.test.ts with a counting Proxy around db() that counts statements naming commerce.bonus_settings, commerce.affiliate and commerce.checkout_rules (0 for a shop-only store), and say so in the hand-back.

Add two cases: with a store whose features are ['shop'], rendering the checkout's pieces does not call readCartBonus (it stays mocked) and the credits part draws nothing; with Bonus on, the cart summary stand-in is asked at most once for one render of the pieces (delivery and credits together).

Append one row with the next free D-number (pull main first; `rg -o '^\| D[0-9]+' docs/decisions.md | tr -dc '0-9\n' | sort -n | tail -1`, plus 1). It records: getCustomer() shared per render (keyed by the session token), the cart count and stock shared per render at their call sites; requestCartSummary() as the one summary of a cart or checkout render; cartSummary() given the store's features so Bonus off and Referrals off send no statement; checkout rules read through a cached list under checkout-rules:{storeId}, refreshed by its four writers; placeOrder() unchanged and still the one that decides, under its own locks. Gift cards are left: cards already sold stay usable while the feature is off. Store-only: Kaizena Flow sells plans through Stripe and draws no cart. No migration.
